etymologies.etymologyHTML: From German Fahrenheit, named after Prussian scientist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit.

definitions.definition: Describing a temperature scale originally defined as having 0°F as the lowest temperature obtainable with a mixture of ice and salt, and 96°F as the temperature of the human body, and now defined with 32°F equal to 0°C, and each degree Fahrenheit equal to 5/9 of a degree Celsius or 5/9 kelvin.

quote.citation: 2017 December 21, Foster Klug, Kim Tong-hyung, Yong Jun Chang, “The cold returns for Winter Games in mountainous Pyeongchang”, in AP News‎[1], archived from the original on February 18, 2024‎[2]:
quote.text: Pyeongchang sits nearly half a mile above sea level in the northeastern corner of South Korea, not too far from the border with the North. It is one of the coldest parts of the country — wind chill in February is often in single digits (Fahrenheit) — and notorious for a powerful, biting wind that gathers force as it barrels down out of Siberia and the Manchurian Plain and then across the jagged granite peaks of North Korea.

quote.citation: 2021, Claire Cock-Starkey, Hyphens & Hashtags, Bodleian Library, page 142:
quote.text: For example, in the Fahrenheit scale 212°F is the boiling point of water.
